question: Should OpenClaw core officially preserve local packaged `dist` mutations and offer guarded opt-in replay after package updates?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but it creates a durable public updater and executable-code security contract that requires maintainer intent rather than automated approval.

options.title: Accept guarded preservation and replay
options.body: Adopt recovery-bundle preservation by default and retain explicit replay with the current fail-closed integrity and topology checks.

options.title: Preserve without replay
options.body: Keep capture, recovery bundles, and user-visible reporting but remove replay mutations and the public flag.

options.title: Decline packaged override support
options.body: Keep packaged installs immutable and continue treating local `dist` edits as outside the supported updater contract.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded preservation and replay
recommendation.body: Adopt recovery-bundle preservation by default and retain explicit replay with the current fail-closed integrity and topology checks.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and repeatedly maintained the core updater and is the live assignee on this PR.
